t:
The Merchant Marine Act, 1920, is amended—

    (1) 
in section 8 (46 U.S.C. App. 867)—

        (A) 
by striking “Interstate Commerce Commission” both places it appears and inserting in lieu thereof “Surface Transportation Board”; and
 
        (B) 
by striking “commission” and inserting in lieu thereof “Board”;
  
    (2) 
in section 27A (46 U.S.C. App. 883–1) by striking “common or contract” and all that follows through “, which otherwise” and inserting in lieu thereof “carrier subject to jurisdiction under subchapter II of chapter 135 of title 49, United States Code, which otherwise”; and
 
    (3) 
in section 28 (46 U.S.C. App. 884)—

        (A) 
by striking “common”;
 
        (B) 
by striking “Interstate Commerce Commission” and inserting in lieu thereof “Surface Transportation Board”; and
 
        (C) 
by striking “commission” each place it appears and inserting in lieu thereof “Board”.

fable.w: This section only makes conforming amendments to the Merchant Marine Act, 1920, substituting the Surface Transportation Board for the Interstate Commerce Commission and adjusting carrier terminology. The tempting reading is that references to a "Board" or "Commission" signal an advisory body or outside consultation, but both are federal agencies and the text creates no comment period, hearing, consultation, rulemaking, or right to sue. No party outside the federal government is brought into any federal decision.
fable.s: by striking “Interstate Commerce Commission” both places it appears and inserting in lieu thereof “Surface Transportation Board”

qwen_block.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to the Merchant Marine Act, specifically replacing references to the 'Interstate Commerce Commission' with the 'Surface Transportation Board' and updating jurisdictional language. It does not establish any new process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, or advisory committees. The changes are purely administrative and internal to the federal government's regulatory structure.

opus.w: This section makes technical conforming amendments to the Merchant Marine Act, 1920, such as replacing "Interstate Commerce Commission" with "Surface Transportation Board" and revising carrier references. It could look like participation because a "Board" is mentioned, but that Board is a federal regulatory agency, not an advisory body with outside members. The section has no comment period, hearing, rulemaking authority, outside consultation, or right to sue.
opus.b: **Step 1: Analysis.** The tempting misreading is to treat the references to a "Board" and a "Commission" as advisory bodies with outside members. But the Surface Transportation Board and the Interstate Commerce Commission are both federal agencies. The section only makes technical conforming amendments: it swaps agency names and changes how carriers are described. Nothing in it brings anyone outside the federal government into a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments updating statutory references from the 'Interstate Commerce Commission' to the 'Surface Transportation Board.' Both are federal agencies, so this is an intra-governmental reorganization. There is no requirement for consultation with, or participation by, any party outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or private entities) in making a decision.

qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that renaming the "Interstate Commerce Commission" to the "Surface Transportation Board" implies a change in how the public participates, or that the Board itself is an advisory body. However, the Surface Transportation Board is a federal agency (inside the government), and this text is purely a technical amendment updating statutory references to reflect a reorganization of federal agencies. It does not create any new process for outside parties to consult with the government, nor does it grant new rights to the public. The actors involved are all federal entities or legal definitions of carriers.
